mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement OM654 engine for a C300d typically costs between £1,200 and £5,500 depending on condition. Used units start from £1,200-£2,800, reconditioned from £2,800-£4,800, and fully rebuilt from £3,000-£5,500. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The C300d uses the OM654 engine, which has a timing chain, not a belt. The chain is generally robust, but individual bolts or chain links of the camshaft timing chain might wear in case of long-term operation under specific driving conditions, potentially leading to a tear. A metallic rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs of engine problems in the C300d include: a 'No Start in XXX miles' countdown warning (AdBlue system failure), reduced power or limp mode (EGR cooler or turbo issues), a rattling noise on cold start (timing chain wear), and coolant leaks or warning lights (coolant pump/vacuum circuit recall issue on 2017-2021 models). If you experience any of these, have the car inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and mileage. A W205 C300d is typically worth £10,000-£22,000 - a rebuilt OM654 engine (£3,000-£5,200) is usually well within the car's value and can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W206 C300d is worth £25,000-£45,000 - a rebuilt OM654.820 engine (£3,200-£5,500) is easily justified. For lower-value examples, an AdBlue or EGR repair is often more economical than a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM654.920 and OM654.820 engines in the C300d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both engines are 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesels from the OM654 family, but with different power outputs and applications. The OM654.920 is used in the W205 C300d (2018-2021), producing 241 hp and 500 Nm of torque. The OM654.820 is used in the W206 C300d (2021-present), producing 261 hp and 550 Nm of torque. The OM654.820 also features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) mild hybrid system.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d AdBlue system to fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AdBlue system on the C300d can fail due to crystallisation in the dosing injector, a failed heater element in the AdBlue tank, or degraded NOx sensors. The ECU responds with a 'No Start in XXX miles' countdown when AdBlue dosing is compromised. Common fault codes include P202E84 (AdBlue metering valve malfunction) and P20F409 (AdBlue consumption too low). Mercedes issued a recall for 2017-2021 models with OM654 engines due to a potential coolant leak between the coolant pump and the vacuum circuit.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C300d badge arrived with the W205 facelift in 2018, replacing the earlier C300 BlueTEC. It introduced Mercedes' all-new OM654 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel - a clean-sheet design that replaced the ageing 3.0-litre V6 OM642 with a lighter, more efficient aluminium-block unit. The C300d was positioned as the flagship four-cylinder diesel, offering V6-rivalling performance with significantly improved economy. The badge continued into the W206 generation in 2021, with power increased to 261 hp.

milestones.description: OM654.920, 2.0L diesel, 241 hp (180 kW) - W205 C300d launch; aluminium block with steel pistons; 500 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 5.7 seconds; 9G-TRONIC automatic
OM654.920 4MATIC variant available; same power output
OM654.820, 2.0L diesel, 261 hp (195 kW) - W206 C300d launch; 550 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 5.4 seconds; integrated starter-generator (ISG) mild hybrid system added
C300d continues with OM654.820; 9G-TRONIC remains standard

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C300d uses Mercedes' modern OM654 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel - a clean-sheet design introduced in 2016 that represents a significant leap forward in diesel technology. While the OM654 is generally more reliable than the older OM651 it replaced, it has well-documented weak points in its emissions control systems. Rebuilt C300d engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM654 AdBlue System Failure - "No Start in XXX Miles" Warnings in the C300d
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d (OM654.920 and OM654.820, W205 and W206, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue (SCR) system components - heater elements, dosing injectors, and NOx sensors - are prone to failure. Mercedes issued a recall for 2017-2021 diesel models fitted with the OM654 engine due to a potential coolant leak between the coolant pump and the vacuum circuit, which could lead to a fire hazard. Common fault codes include P202E84 (AdBlue metering valve malfunction) and P20F409 (AdBlue consumption too low).

repairOptions.tier: AdBlue Tank Heater or Injector Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed heater element or dosing injector, clear fault codes, perform SCR reset
repairOptions.longevity: Requires specialist diagnostic tools to identify the exact component

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace upstream and/or downstream NOx sensors, ECU software update
repairOptions.longevity: Common on 2018-2022 models; sensors have a limited service life

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with updated emissions components and injectors
repairOptions.longevity: Only if engine has been run with repeated SCR failures causing EGR clogging

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W205 C300d is worth £10,000-£22,000, while a W206 C300d is worth £25,000-£45,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £15,000, an AdBlue repair (£600-£1,300) is almost always the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt OM654 with warranty (£3,000-£5,500) offers peace of mind. The C300d's strong retained values mean replacement is usually justified for well-maintained cars.
problems.recommendation: When the countdown appears, don't ignore it. A mobile AdBlue specialist can often diagnose and repair heater or injector faults for half the dealer cost. For vehicles over 100,000 miles facing repeated SCR issues, compare the cost of repairs against replacement. If you're seeing both P13E400 (limited remaining driving distance due to AdBlue malfunction) and P229F8S (NOx sensor malfunction), start with the NOx sensors.

problems.group: OM654 EGR Cooler & Vacuum System Failure
problems.h4: OM654 EGR Cooler & Vacuum System Failure - Reduced Power and Hesitation
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d (OM654.920 and OM654.820, W205 and W206, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: The EGR system on the OM654 can suffer from carbon buildup, particularly on vehicles used for short urban journeys. The EGR cooler vacuum diaphragm can fail, causing underboost issues (fault code P0299). The vacuum actuator can fail repeatedly due to debris from the exhaust system abrading the silicone boot.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve and associated pipes; or replace if necessary
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; cleaning often sufficient

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace vacuum diaphragm on EGR cooler, check solenoid operation
repairOptions.longevity: Ensure control solenoid is also checked; debris may be causing repeat failures

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with upgraded EGR components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if EGR issues have caused significant engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your C300d experiences hesitation, limp mode, or the engine management light comes on with EGR-related codes (P0299), have the system inspected promptly. A £300-£600 specialist EGR clean is far cheaper than a £3,000 engine replacement. Regular motorway driving helps keep the EGR system clear. If the vacuum diaphragm fails repeatedly, have the control solenoid and exhaust port filter checked.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM654 EGR system repair and engine replacement for your C300d

problems.h4: OM654 Timing Chain Wear - Camshaft Timing Chain Durability Concerns
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300d (OM654.920 and OM654.820, W205 and W206, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: The OM654 uses a timing chain that is generally robust, but individual bolts or chain links of the camshaft timing chain might wear in case of long-term operation under specific driving conditions. In this case, the durability of the camshaft timing chain might be impaired over time and subsequently lead to a tear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect timing chain and tensioner; perform diagnostic checks
repairOptions.longevity: Essential if rattling noise is heard on start-up

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has stretched or is showing wear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new chain and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has failed or caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: The OM654's timing chain is generally robust, but if you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold start - particularly on higher-mileage cars - have it inspected immediately. Use the correct Mercedes-approved oil spec and change it every 10,000 miles to maximise chain life.

problems.group: OM654 Coolant Pump & Vacuum Circuit Recall
problems.h4: OM654 Coolant Pump & Vacuum Circuit Recall - Fire Risk on 2017-2021 Models
problems.rootCause: A leak may develop between the coolant pump and the vacuum circuit, allowing coolant to enter the vacuum circuit. This can affect components and result in an increase in temperature, potentially leading to a vehicle fire. Mercedes issued a recall for 2017-2021 models with OM654 and OM656 engines addressing this issue.

repairOptions.longevity: Check if recall has been performed on your vehicle

For vehicles over 100,000 miles facing repeated SCR issues, compare the cost of repairs against replacement. If you're seeing both P13E400 (limited remaining driving distance due to AdBlue malfunction) and P229F8S (NOx sensor malfunction), start with the NOx sensors.
